title: TraceLab: Characterizing Coding Agent Workloads for LLM Serving
finding: 4,265 Claude Code/Codex sessions (43 users): 95.7% of 54.9B input tokens were cache-read prefix; prefix tokens = 59.5% of list-price cost, append 29.2%, output 11.2%; tool-result steps hit 97.5%, user-turn steps 84.4%; misses mainly after human pauses >TTL; tool latency heavy-tailed (median 0.3s, p99 3.6min)
applicability: high (cost-share structure mirrors our 66% cache-read finding; shows it is the normal regime)
limitation: self-collected single team, list-price estimates not bills; system prompt/tool-definition share NOT reported; eviction idealised

title: Agentic AI Workload Characteristics
finding: ReAct-style Claude Code harness on Qwen3.6-27B/Gemma4-31B, 5 benchmarks: empirical cache-hit 84.6-99.5%; decode 91-98.6% of LLM time; prefill 1.4-9%; thrashing drops hit to 16-26% and throughput up to 66%; tools 2-29% of runtime
applicability: med (latency/throughput not billing)
limitation: two open models self-hosted, no money accounting, tool-def share not reported

title: Continuum: KV Cache Time-to-Live for multi-turn agent scheduling
finding: Pinning KV across tool calls with TTL cuts delay 1.12-3.66x (up to 8.18x) vs vLLM/InferCept/Autellix on SWE-bench and BFCL traces with Llama-3.1 8B/70B; tool durations long-tailed (SWE mean 0.9s)
applicability: med: latency/throughput for self-hosters, not price; requires engine control
limitation: no hit-rate report, no hosted API eval, no tool-def discussion; Llama only

title: Manus: Context Engineering for AI Agents (Yichao Ji)
finding: KV-cache hit rate is 'the single most important metric'; avoid adding/removing tools mid-iteration; mask logits instead of removing tools; claims 10x price gap cached vs uncached (Sonnet)
applicability: high (direct counter-position to dynamic tool exposure)
limitation: no data published; not read in full (snippet-level)

title: Don't Break the Cache: Evaluation of Prompt Caching for Long-Horizon Agentic Tasks (Lumer et al.)
finding: DeepResearch Bench, 40 sessions/condition/model, 10k-token system prompt: cost cut 78-81% (GPT-5.2, Sonnet 4.5), 28-48% (Gemini 2.5 Pro, GPT-4o); dynamic tool set invalidates the prefix; Claude TTFT benefit shrank from 19% at 3 tools to 5% at 50 tools; GPT-4o full-context caching increased latency
applicability: high (billed-cost with cache write/read accounted, per provider)
limitation: one benchmark, small n, Jan-2026 prices, fixed system prompt; web-search tools not AppWorld

title: Anthropic docs: Tool use with prompt caching
finding: Prefix order tools->system->messages; modifying tool defs invalidates entire cache; tool_choice change invalidates messages cache; defer_loading/tool_search appends discovered tool as tool_reference in history so prefix cache preserved
applicability: high
limitation: Anthropic only; describes behaviour, no measurements

title: OpenRouter prompt caching docs
finding: Cache read 0.1x-0.5x of input by provider; DeepSeek write=input price, Z.AI (GLM) writes free 'limited-time' reads ~0.2x; sticky routing per conversation hash (60 min), session_id header improves hit; MiniMax not mentioned; OpenAI GPT-5.6+ bills cache writes
applicability: high (our routes)
limitation: pricing varies by provider/time; no measured hit rates

title: DeepSeek API docs: context caching on disk
finding: Prefix-unit based, best-effort, no hit guarantee, TTL hours to days; usage reports hit/miss tokens
applicability: med
limitation: DeepSeek only; page lacked pricing

title: How Do Coding Agents Spend Your Money? (token consumption in agentic coding)
finding: OpenHands on SWE-bench Verified (500x4 runs, 8 models): cache reads are the largest token and dollar category in every phase; same-task runs differ up to 30x in tokens (avg most/least expensive run ~2x); cost computed with cache-write/read rates
applicability: high (independent confirmation of cache-read dominance; run variance relevant to our noise)
limitation: no numeric split in text (figure only); tool-def tokens not separated; SWE-bench not AppWorld; inconsistent 1000x/3500x claims

title: OpenRouter Inferred #3 'Cache is Crucial'
finding: Cached share of agentic prompt tokens ~60% (Jan 2026) -> just under 90% (Sep 2026); median provider cache rate 44% -> 85%; Z.ai, DeepSeek, OpenAI >90%; example: cached tokens ~87% of tokens but ~1/3 of the bill at 1/10 price
applicability: high (our route is OpenRouter; gives provider-level hit rates and the 'tokens vs money' framing)
limitation: OpenRouter's own classification of keys, no external validation; list prices Oct 2026; averages hide per-provider variance

title: Blog: same prompt 0 to 91% hit rates (sm1ck)
finding: Companion-chat 5K prefix, 10 follow-ups, ~4 weeks via OpenRouter: hit 91% (Cydonia), 75% (Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite, only with marker), 51% (Grok); 0% below min prefix length
applicability: low-med (shows hit rate is provider- and config-specific)
limitation: single operator, no n, chat not agent

title: Tail-Replay: prefix caching for hybrid linear-attention LLMs
finding: Prefix caching on hybrid linear-attention models is not a plain token-prefix match; engines need special handling
applicability: med (self-hosted vLLM + model architecture may cap hit rate; MiniMax-M3 architecture unchecked)
limitation: not read

title: KVFlow (prefix caching for multi-agent workflows)
finding: Workflow-aware eviction: up to 1.83x over SGLang hierarchical radix cache (single workflow), 2.19x concurrent
applicability: low (latency)
limitation: not read

title: LLMCompiler / AsyncLM / PASTE (parallel, async, speculative tool calls)
finding: Reduce number of sequential LLM requests or hide tool latency: LLMCompiler up to 3.7x latency, 6.7x cost (token-based, not cache-aware); AsyncLM 1.6-5.4x latency; PASTE -48.5% completion time
applicability: med (they attack the 'wait' framing and the number of requests, but are latency claims; 'cost' in LLMCompiler is from token counts)
limitation: not read; cost claim not cache-aware

title: AgentServeSim / SAGA
finding: Program-level KV retention/scheduling: SAGA 1.64x task completion vs vLLM prefix caching; simulator within ~5% JCT
applicability: low
limitation: latency/throughput only; self-reported

title: Serving GLM-5.2 for Agentic Workloads on llm-d (Red Hat/IBM)
finding: On 219 real Claude Code sessions (SemiAnalysis/Weka traces): 96% of requests reuse >=90% of input as verbatim prefix (median 99.6%); median request only 632 tokens longer than previous; p50 gap 2s, p90 24s; GLM-5.2 on 64 GPUs got ~90-92% GPU prefix hit rate; implied GPU-rental cost $0.05-0.08/M input vs Z.ai list $1.40/M
applicability: high for self-host and for GLM-family; shows prefix reuse is the dominant structure of agent traffic and that provider list price >> marginal serving cost
limitation: vendor-authored; trace populations differ between stats and benchmark; rental cost at 24/7 utilisation

title: KVCache Cache in the Wild (Alibaba Tongyi; USENIX ATC 2025)
finding: Production traces: ideal hit ratio 54-62% (not 80%+ of synthetic); to-B API traffic is ~single-turn, reuse within seconds; ~10% of blocks give 77% of reuse; most hits same-user; workload-aware eviction +8-24% hit rate in vLLM
applicability: med (shows hit rates are workload-specific; not agent loops)
limitation: no agent/tool workloads; reconstructed token inputs

title: InferCept
finding: Recompute of context at tool-call interception = 37-40% of forward time in vanilla engines; 1.6-2x throughput
applicability: low-med (explains why engines without APC/interception support waste compute; modern APC already avoids)
limitation: 2024 baselines predate APC default

title: vLLM automatic prefix caching design doc
finding: Per-block hash chained over parent hash + tokens (+LoRA/mm/cache_salt); only full blocks cached; LRU eviction; any token change earlier in prompt invalidates all later blocks
applicability: high for university vLLM (tool array rendered by chat template before conversation => subset change = full miss)
limitation: doc says nothing on tools, hybrid models or hit-rate metrics

title: OpenAI prompt caching guide
finding: Tool names/descriptions/schemas/ordering changes break reuse from that point; recommends stable tools + tool_choice/allowed_tools restriction; GPT-5.6+ bills cache writes (1.25x for 30 min) and reads at 0.1x; older models no write fee
applicability: high (gpt-5-mini route; exactly the 'fixed offering' pattern)
limitation: pricing differs by model generation

title: MCP client best practices (progressive discovery, prompt caching)
finding: Changing tool list mid-conversation invalidates cached prefix and 'can cost more tokens than the definitions removed'; append new definitions after breakpoint or use a stable call_tool meta-tool; thresholds for switching to discovery at 1-5% of context
applicability: high (policy design guidance)
limitation: no measurement behind the claim

title: exe.dev 'Expensively quadratic'
finding: One Anthropic-priced conversation: cache reads 87% of cost at end; cache reads reach 50% of cost at ~27.5k tokens context; cost scales with tokens x calls
applicability: med (arithmetic of re-sending; confirms the supervisor's 'you pay each request' as cache-read cost)
limitation: single conversation headline; Opus 4.5 prices

title: SiliconFlow / Novita interleaved-thinking guides
finding: reasoning_content must be replayed exactly across turns for GLM-4.7/DeepSeek V3.2; omission lowers cache efficiency and quality
applicability: med (MiniMax/GLM harness correctness)
limitation: no measurement; snippet-level
